sections.name: COUNTRY_CENTROIDS (part 1)
sections.title: Country coordinates, first half
sections.what: Lists countries from the United States through Taiwan with a rough centre latitude, longitude and display name.
sections.why: Gives the map one point for each country the app can place.
sections.watch_out: Two codes, UK and GB, both point to the United Kingdom, so the same country can appear under two keys.

sections.name: COUNTRY_CENTROIDS (part 2)
sections.title: Country coordinates, second half
sections.what: Continues the table from Singapore to Serbia with the same kind of entries.
sections.why: Completes the list of countries the app can place on a map.
sections.watch_out: Countries not in the table cannot be placed, and no fallback is shown here.

sections.name: resolveCountryCode
sections.title: Finding a country code from a name
sections.what: Turns a country name or code into the standard code. It tries an exact code, then an exact name, then a partial name match. It returns nothing if none of these work.
sections.why: Input often comes as a name from a web page, so the helper converts it to a code the rest of the app can use.
sections.watch_out: The partial match runs in table order, so an input such as 'Niger' matches 'Nigeria' because Niger is missing from the table.

summary: A fixed table of country codes, names and approximate centre points, plus a helper that turns a country name or code into the standard code.
purpose: Lets the app place projects on a map when it only knows the country, by giving each country one approximate point.
why: Likely reason: a rough centre point per country is enough for a map view, so the code keeps it simple instead of using boundary shapes.
how: The table maps each code to a latitude, a longitude and a display name. The helper takes the input, trims it, uppercases it and looks for a direct code match, then a name match, then a partial name match.
inputs: A country name or code as text, or nothing.
outputs: The standard two-letter code for the country, or nothing when no match is found. The table itself gives coordinates and names.
risks: The partial name match can pick the wrong country. For example, 'Niger' is not in the table, so it can match 'Nigeria' by partial name. Some codes, such as UK, are not standard ISO codes.
debug: If a project appears in the wrong place, check what text the country came from and run it through the helper. If a country is missing from the map, check whether it is in the table.
